misconceptions.description: Believing that positive, general comments ("looks great") count as a completed peer review
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer leaves only praise or vague reactions with no specific, actionable note
misconceptions.feedback: Useful review names a location, the problem, and a concrete fix. "Looks great" gives the writer nothing to act on.

misconceptions.description: Taking over a peer's document by rewriting passages instead of flagging issues for them to decide on
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer replaces the writer's wording rather than raising a question or suggestion
misconceptions.feedback: Keep ownership with the writer. Raise concerns as questions or suggestions, not as a takeover of their voice.

misconceptions.description: Pasting a peer's resume, including personal contact details, into a third-party tool without permission
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer submits another person's identifying data to an AI tool during review
misconceptions.feedback: Peer review carries a duty of care. Strip identifying details before using any third-party tool, and get consent.

misconceptions.description: Treating every peer comment as a required edit instead of judging each against the goal
misconceptions.trigger: writer applies all comments verbatim or rejects all of them without reasons
misconceptions.feedback: Judge each comment against your goal. Act on the ones that fit, decline the rest with a reason, and log the decisions.
